messages:
maria: Heads-up — after bumping eu-west to 25% for model v2.3 we’re seeing a small but steady rise in 5xxs. Putting a safety latch on the rollout. Can folks weigh in: hold/pin/rollback?

deploy-bot: Deploy Event: staged-rollout v2.3 -> eu-west, target 25% traffic. current: 25% (started by maria)

josh: saw it too. error rate +0.9% over baseline for last 12m, p95 latency up ~40ms. Not huge but trending. Do we have recent infra noise?

rachael: quick check of the node pool shows occasional pod restarts on node pool eu-workers-3. Logs show repeated kubelet OOM warnings around the same timeframe. Could be unrelated but suspicious.

maria: thanks. timeline? when did the node restarts start relative to traffic bump?

rachael: restarts started ~8m before the bump; frequency increased after we raised to 25%. Might be longer-lived state hitting some mem edge when KV cache warms under new seq length distribution.

sam: suggestion: don't fully rollback global. Hold EU rollout, pin eu routing to v2.2 (previous stable) while infra investigates. We can keep collection of request samples for evaluation.

josh: +1 for targeted pin. Quick operational plan: 1) set eu region routing override to v2.2 2) reduce EU traffic to 10% to buy time 3) run replay on failing requests to reproduce. Who can run the pin?

maria: I can do the routing override. josh, can you run the replay and fetch detailed traces?

josh: on it. grabbing traces and will run the replay job. Command I’ll use:```bash
./infra/tools/replay --from=2026-03-20T10:42Z --region=eu-west --filter=status>=500 --limit=2000
```

maria: doing the routing override now. Pin config change: `/routes set --region eu-west --model v2.2 --sticky true --note "safety latch after 5xx uptick"`

deploy-bot: Route change: eu-west pinned to v2.2 by maria. Traffic target updated -> 10% (manual override).

ops-bot: Canary health snapshot: errors 5xx=1.8% (up from 0.9%), p95 latency=540ms (baseline 500ms), cpu usage nodes +12%.

rachael: I’ll open a quick infra incident and attach node kubelet logs. If this is KV-cache related we may need a runtime patch (reduce cache size or bump pod memory) rather than model rollback.

maria: agree. we shouldn’t roll back model globally until we root cause infra vs model. pinning EU to v2.2 and dropping to 10% gives us margin. Does anyone oppose?

sam: :thumbsup: fine by me. we should also flag eval/QA to run targeted prompts that previously regressed.

josh: replay started — will post artifacts in ~15m. If replay reproduces client-facing 5xxs we’ll escalate rollback plan (traffic cut to 0% for eu-west).

maria: note for release notes / postmortem: mark this as "safety latch engaged: eu-west pinned to v2.2 due to elevated 5xx rate after v2.3 bump." I'll add to the release doc and notify customers on the EU beta list.

deploy-bot: Incident ticket created #INC-1254 (owner: rachael).

rachael: adding initial analysis to INC-1254: node restarts correlate with increased KV cache allocations under v2.3. Investigating pod memory pressure and tokenizer path.

josh: replay artifacts: https://artifacts.internal/replays/3801234567/ — see failures caused by grpc timeout to runtime-proxy, stack trace snippet attached in artifacts.

maria: thanks. team consensus: hold rollout, eu pinned to v2.2, infra investigating. We'll reconvene in 30m unless new signal appears. If any stakeholder wants faster rollback to 0% for eu-west, call it now.

sam: noted. will ping QA and support to watch EU error alerts and pause any external comms until we have more.

maria: closing loop — pin enforced, observability alerts dialed up, incident created. Thanks all. :heart:

ops-bot: Rolling log: pinned eu-west -> v2.2 (maria) | incident INC-1254 opened (rachael) | replay job 1532 started (josh)

maria: (follow-up) after infra fixes we’ll attempt a controlled re-bump to 10% with additional KV cache limits and memory headroom, then evaluate over 1h before any further increase.

josh: +1. will post replay summary and suggested mitigations in INC-1254.

rachael: provisional mitigation checklist added to incident: [increase pod mem, enable per-pod cache cap, continue node pool health checks].

maria: thanks everyone — holding this thread open for updates.
